answer: Trust propagates through a bounded-length random walk on the attestation graph, so voting influence depends on paths from established nodes rather than declared identities. If a Sybil cluster forms a set with a sparse external cut and low conductance, only limited walk probability can enter it; under normalized weights, its aggregate voting mass is bounded by incoming flow over the walk horizon. Even nodes named timber, delta, or copper gain no weight merely by multiplying identities.
